rivals.why: Classic head-to-head: both sell subscription policy content plus online training and wellness to the same public safety chief for compliance and liability reduction
Both sell shift scheduling and workforce management to the same police, corrections and 911 scheduling administrator
Cloud shift scheduling for police and dispatch, directly substituting for Vector's scheduling module for the same buyer
Benchmark's performance management and early intervention overlaps Guardian Tracking, sold to the same professional standards command

rival:vector-solutions.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:vector-solutions.why: Vector is a bundle, so its rivals differ by module: Lexipol on training and policy content, InTime and Pace on scheduling, Benchmark on performance and early intervention. I excluded every simulator vendor (VirTra, MILO, Apex, InVeris, Kaiden) - hardware and scenario simulators are a separate capital purchase from an online compliance LMS, and an agency buys both.

rivals.why: Veritone iDEMS is a digital evidence management system sold to the same agency evidence and records custodian
Both sell digital evidence management to the same public safety evidence unit consolidating media from many sources
Axon Evidence is the incumbent digital evidence cloud VeriPic sells against for the same department's evidence storage and sharing decision
BEAST covers the physical property and evidence room VeriPic also handles, competing for the same property unit's chain-of-custody system

rival:veripic.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:veripic.why: VeriPic spans digital and physical evidence, so the shortlist includes both the DEMS vendors and the property-room system. Excluded the camera makers (LensLock, Digital Ally, Getac) - their evidence cloud comes bundled with a hardware purchase, a different procurement, and excluded CaseGuard/Pimloc, which redact evidence rather than manage it.

rivals.why: Both sell digital evidence management to the same public safety agency consolidating and disclosing case media
Axon's digital evidence cloud plus its redaction tools compete with iDEMS and Redact for the same department's evidence workflow
Digital evidence management for law enforcement, an either/or purchase against iDEMS for the same evidence custodian
CaseGuard Studio is AI audio/video redaction sold to the same police records unit facing public records requests as Veritone Redact
AI video redaction and privacy software competing directly with Veritone Redact for the same disclosure and FOIA workload
BriefCam's video review and object search is the alternative to Veritone Track for the same investigator scanning hours of footage

rival:veritone.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:veritone.why: Veritone sells three distinct public safety apps, and each has its own rival set: iDEMS against NICE/Axon/VeriPic, Redact against CaseGuard/Pimloc, Track against BriefCam. Every edge names a specific product overlap rather than the aiWARE brand.

rival:verkada.evidence: All four sell the camera-and-VMS (and in Genetec's and Motorola's case, access control) stack that a SLED physical security buyer chooses among. A district or city standardizes on one platform.

rivals.why: Security Center VMS plus access control is the direct alternative to Verkada's cloud cameras and access control for the same city or campus security buyer
XProtect video management competes for the same agency's camera system decision - open platform versus Verkada's cloud appliance
Avigilon video security is bid against Verkada for the same municipal and school district surveillance deployment
Surveillance cameras and video analytics sold to the same public agency physical security procurement

rival:verkada.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:verkada.why: Held this to the video surveillance platform vendors. Per the worked example, cameras are not a data platform: Palantir, Peregrine, Flock and SoundThinking are all bought alongside Verkada, never instead of it. Also excluded BriefCam and LiveView - analytics layered on a VMS and solar trailer units are complements, not substitutes.

rival:versaterm.evidence: Each sells an integrated CAD and/or RMS platform to a police agency that will run exactly one. Versaterm's stated strategy of growing a public safety suite via acquisitions is the same land-grab CentralSquare, Motorola and Hexagon are running against the same customer base.

rivals.why: Big-three CAD/911/RMS suite bid head-to-head with Versaterm for the same mid and large agency records and dispatch replacement
Cloud-native CAD and RMS competing for the same modern-platform agency migrating off legacy records systems
Enterprise CAD, dispatch and records for large police departments and 911 centers - the same suite decision Versaterm bids
Motorola's 911 call handling and CAD suite competes for the same large agency dispatch and records platform award
NicheRMS365 targets the same large and multi-agency forces in North America, UK and Australia for one shared records system
Cloud CAD, RMS and jail management sold to the same law enforcement agency consolidating onto a single suite

rival:versaterm.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:versaterm.why: Versaterm sits in the enterprise and multi-agency tier, so its shortlist is the big platform vendors rather than the small-agency browser suites (eFORCE, ProPhoenix, Sun Ridge, Southern Software) that Valor competes with.

rival:videray-technologies.evidence: No other roster company sells through-object imaging. The nearest names solve different problems: Berkeley Varitronics detects RF from contraband cellphones (a signal, not an image, and only for phones), Bounce Imaging throws a 360 camera into a room to see the space rather than inside a package, and Boston Dynamics Spot is a robot platform a bomb squad carries the imager on - a complement Videray would mount to, not a substitute.
rival:videray-technologies.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:videray-technologies.why: A bomb squad or corrections unit buying a handheld backscatter X-ray imager has no alternative on this roster. Adjacency to contraband detection and bomb squads is not competition; listing Berkeley Varitronics or Bounce Imaging here would be exactly the Robin Radar/Brinc error.

rival:virtra.evidence: VirTra, MILO Range and InVeris FATS are the three names on essentially every judgmental use-of-force simulator RFP - same product category, same police academy and training division buyer, one capital purchase. Apex Officer and Kaiden AI attack that same purchase with VR and AI-voice alternatives.

rivals.why: Interactive use-of-force and firearms training simulators - the direct head-to-head bid against VirTra for the same academy training budget
FATS virtual training systems are the legacy incumbent judgmental simulator agencies evaluate against VirTra
VR use-of-force and de-escalation training simulators sold to the same police training commander as an alternative simulator format
AI-voiced de-escalation scenario training competes for the same academy de-escalation training dollars as a software-only alternative to a screen-and-projector simulator

rival:virtra.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:virtra.why: A tight, real cluster. Excluded Vector Solutions and Lexipol - an online training LMS and policy subscription is a separate recurring purchase that sits alongside a simulator, not instead of one.

rivals.why: Axon's TASER is the incumbent less-lethal remote-incapacitation tool BolaWrap is bid against for the same department's less-lethal equipment budget and use-of-force policy decision

rival:wrap-technologies.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:wrap-technologies.why: Wrap is close to alone here. Axon is the one real edge: both sell a handheld device an officer deploys at distance to subdue a subject without lethal force, to the same chief and the same equipment line. Excluded StarChase, which also avoids escalation but solves vehicle pursuit rather than subject restraint, and excluded every simulator vendor - training on use of force is not a substitute for the device.
